mr_description: May your database queries be much reduced with minimal effort.

expected_issues.title: from_db() always called with fetch_mode, breaking documented overrides
expected_issues.description:
Model.from_db() is now always called with a new fetch_mode keyword, which raises TypeError for models overriding from_db() with the documented signature from_db(cls, db, field_names, values).

from_db() is a documented, overridable classmethod. ModelIterable and RawModelIterable now pass `fetch_mode=` unconditionally, so any project overriding from_db() with the previously documented four-argument signature crashes on every query of that model. A backward-compatible path (detect whether the override accepts fetch_mode/**kwargs, call the old signature and emit a deprecation warning) is needed.

expected_issues.title: FETCH_PEERS assigns one-element tuples to scalar fields
expected_issues.description: fetch_many() calls values_list(attname) without flat=True. This snapshot supports in_bulk() on values-list querysets and removes its added key column, leaving a one-element tuple as each value. setattr() therefore stores (value,) in the deferred scalar field rather than value when peer fetching runs. Use flat=True so bulk-loaded scalar fields retain their normal types.
